children: US stock indices closed lower on Tuesday under continued pressure from higher bond yields.
The S&P 500 fell 0.4%, the Dow shed 328 points and the Nasdaq lost 0.6%.
The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield hit its highest level in nearly two decades.
Escalating Middle East strikes worsened the outlook for regional energy supplies, increasing inflation risks and the prospect of a hawkish Federal Reserve response.
Markets expect the Fed to hike rates by 25 bps tomorrow as higher fuel prices have driven inflationary pressures this year.
Losses were broad-based, with credit-sensitive AI hyperscalers hit by rising borrowing costs.
Alphabet shed 1.3%, Microsoft lost 1.6%, Oracle tumbled 3.1% and Amazon retreated 2%.
Chipmakers were mostly higher following Monday’s selloff, when Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for slower AI development to mitigate risks from increasingly capable models.

title: US Stocks Drop as Yields Extend Surge
